title: Best Time to Buy And Sell Stock
statement: You get the price of one stock for each day. Pick one day to buy and a later day to sell. Return the largest profit you can make. If every possible trade loses money, return 0.

example.caption: Buy on day 1 at 1, sell on day 4 at 6. Profit is 5. Buying at 7 first would never pay off.

idea.sentence: Treat buy and sell as the two ends of a window. Walk the sell end forward, and whenever a cheaper day appears, jump the buy end to it.

jargon.plain: A stretch of the array between two markers. Both markers only ever move forward.
The lowest value seen so far while walking left to right.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the list of daily prices, e.g. [7,1,5,3,6,4]

compare.bruteLabel: Try every buy and sell pair
compare.optimalLabel: One pass, remember the cheapest day

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: For each buy day, look at every later sell day.

rows.name: One pass
rows.note: Each day is visited once. Only the buy index and the best profit are stored.

fast.takeaway: The best buy day for any sell day is just the lowest price before it. Remember that one number instead of rechecking all earlier days.

stages.title: Start the window
stages.note: Buy day 0. The best profit so far is 0, which also covers the no-trade case.

stages.title: Cheaper day: move buy
stages.note: If today is cheaper than the buy day, it is a better buy day for everything after it.

stages.title: Otherwise try selling
stages.note: Profit is today's price minus the buy price. Keep the larger profit.

stages.title: Return the best
stages.note: After the last day, the best profit is the answer. It stays 0 if prices only fall.

edges.title: Prices only fall
edges.why: Every trade loses money, so the best move is not to trade. The best starts at 0 and never grows.

edges.title: Single day
edges.why: You cannot sell on a later day. The loop never runs and 0 is returned.

edges.title: Low comes after the high
edges.why: The cheapest price is 1, but it is last. Buying there allows no sale. Selling must come after buying.

edges.title: Equal prices
edges.why: Same price on every day gives profit 0. Equal is not cheaper, so the buy day stays.

gotchas.text: Do not take max(prices) minus min(prices). The minimum may come after the maximum, and you cannot sell before you buy.
Start best at 0, not at a negative number or the first price. A losing-only list must return 0.
Math.min(...prices) spreads the whole array into arguments. It can crash with a stack error on very large arrays. A plain loop is safe.
The built-in max needs Go 1.21 or newer. On older versions write the comparison with an if.

recap.key: Walk the sell day forward. Keep the cheapest day so far as the buy day, and track the best price difference.
moves: Start with buy at day 0 and best at 0
If today is cheaper than the buy day, move buy here
Otherwise profit is today minus buy. Keep the larger
Return best, which is 0 if no trade pays
